claim: The target experiment is same-dataset, position-to-position HAR using 81 features per body part and shared activity labels.
DAPCA has a published MATLAB implementation and accepts labeled source features with unlabeled target features, returning a joint linear projection.
DAPCA is structurally compatible with the project's feature-level CPAR task; this is a fit inference, not a previously published result on this benchmark.
DAPCA is not validated by its cited paper on this exact HAR benchmark, and its repository declares GPL-3.0.
ICSC uses iterative confident pseudo-labeling and has MATLAB source code.
The public ICSC method function receives target truth for internal accuracy reporting, so a target-label-blind experiment should move scoring outside the method.
The public ICSC code assumes class IDs 1 through C in its class-mean loop; nonconsecutive activity IDs require consistent remapping.
Xu et al. (2023) is directly about cross-position HAR but uses a deep CNN/DANN-or-DDC/OS-ELM setup with a few annotated target samples; no MATLAB .m release was verified in this search.
ActiLabel has cross-location HAR experiments but no public MATLAB .m implementation was verified in this search.
DomainATM is a 2023 MATLAB toolbox that includes established algorithms; the toolbox publication date does not make its underlying algorithms recent.
The current SOT code is Python and its published benchmark differs from the project's within-dataset position tasks in class/feature/task setup.
SWL-Adapt is a recent cross-user HAR paper but its public implementation uses Python/PyTorch, not MATLAB .m.
The current demo is transductive if it adapts on all target features and reports performance on those same samples, while target labels remain withheld during adaptation.
Wearing-diversity adaptation performance is sensitive to dataset structure and assumptions, so paper results should not be transplanted as expected scores for this benchmark.
